captive_summary: EG LNG's single-train liquefaction plant at Punta Europa, Bioko Island (operating since 2007) necessarily has significant compression/power demand, but no public source found in extensive searching discloses whether that demand is met by on-site gas turbines/generators or by grid/utility supply. Absence of a published spec is INSUFFICIENT, never a documented NO.
confirmed_how: eglng.com's own About-Us and Technology pages contain only corporate/CSR content, no equipment detail. Wikipedia's Bioko article confirms only that 'the majority of the residue gas from the Alba plant is delivered to a natural gas liquefaction plant operated by EG LNG,' with no machinery detail. LNG Prime's 2025-2026 EG LNG coverage (ConocoPhillips' first-cargo and offtake-deal articles, e.g. https://lngprime.com/lng-terminals/conocophillips-loads-its-first-equatorial-guinea-lng-cargo/154026/) covers commercial matters only and was confirmed (via WebFetch) to contain no capacity, trains, equipment, or power-generation detail. No vendor press release (GE/Baker Hughes/Siemens/MAN), EPC release, or technical paper describing EG LNG's compressor drivers or power plant was located via gCaptain, LNG Prime, or Hydrocarbon Engineering site searches. Not citing any of these as a captive-power finding since none contains the value.
gogpt_prior_assessment: gogpt_prior = yes; nearest plant Malabo Turbogas power plant (154 MW, gogpt_captive=False, 1.996 km away). Malabo Turbogas reads as Equatorial Guinea's public grid power plant serving Malabo city (the Bioko Island capital, adjoining Punta Europa), not a dedicated/fenceline asset of EG LNG's liquefaction plant — the proximity is coincidental to both sites sitting at the edge of the same city. No independent non-gem.wiki source describing Malabo Turbogas specifically was found (searches on LNG Prime and Mojeek returned nothing), so this assessment rests on the public-utility framing implied by the plant's own name/GOGPT's captive=False determination rather than a freshly-sourced citation.
gogpt_candidate_basis: The existence of any dedicated on-site generation at Punta Europa/EG LNG itself is unconfirmed (verdict INSUFFICIENT) — there is nothing to ADD or a basis to definitively rule DO NOT ADD until the underlying captive-power question is resolved with a source.

hardware_summary: 2x Rolls-Royce Bergen B35:40V20AG gas-fueled reciprocating engines for on-board power generation, per the design confirmed built on sister conversion vessel Hilli Episeyo and contractually optioned for Gimi specifically in the same 2015 shipyard/engine contract; MW rating not stated in the source found, and the as-built Gimi configuration (post-2023 conversion) is not independently confirmed.
fuel_basis: gCaptain/Rolls-Royce, Mar 20, 2015: the Bergen B35:40V20AG engines installed on Hilli are 'fueled exclusively by LNG'; the same release states the contract 'includes an option for additional two engines for a second Golar LNG carrier to be converted, Gimi.'
captive_summary: Gimi FLNG (BP-chartered, moored offshore at the Tortue field, converted from a 1976-built Moss-type LNG carrier, operational 2025, 2.7 mtpa nameplate/2.45 mtpa output per Golar's own fleet page) is an off-grid moored FLNG facility that must generate all of its own electric power for liquefaction, utilities and crew — the brief's own grid-access prior for moored FLNG/FSRU vessels. Golar's FLNG conversion design uses gas-fired Bergen dual-fuel gensets for exactly this purpose, confirmed installed on sister vessel Hilli and contractually optioned for Gimi by name in the same 2015 contract. Verdict is YES at yellow confidence: the fuel/equipment class is documented and vessel-specific (not merely inferred), but the as-built Gimi confirmation is a 2015 option rather than a post-conversion disclosure, so it falls short of a second independent, vessel-specific, as-built source.
confirmed_how: gCaptain's Mar 20, 2015 'Rolls-Royce to Power Golar's New Floating LNG Liquefaction Ship' (reporting Rolls-Royce's own release) states two Bergen B35:40V20AG engines were installed on Hilli 'to supply the on-board power generation for the vessel,' fueled exclusively by LNG, powering 'the liquefaction processes, and also for supporting vessel operation and the energy needs of the crew onboard' — and that the same contract 'includes an option for additional two engines for a second Golar LNG carrier to be converted, Gimi.' LNG Prime's Aug 12, 2022 'Golar says Gimi FLNG 86 percent complete' confirms the Gimi conversion was underway at that yard/program. Golar's own fleet page (golarlng.com/fleet.aspx) confirms Gimi: 'Built 1976, Converted 2023,' operational from 2025, 2.7/2.45 mtpa, chartered to BP through 2045 — corroborating the vessel and deployment but not restating the power-plant equipment. The Gimi-specific power-system confirmation therefore rests on the 2015 option language plus the strong physical necessity of self-generation for a moored FLNG vessel, not a post-conversion as-built spec sheet — hence yellow, not green.

verification_log.note: confirms Bergen B35:40V20AG engines and Gimi option
confirms Gimi conversion progress at Keppel
confirms Gimi build/convert years, capacity, BP charter to 2045

gogpt_prior_assessment: gogpt_prior = no; no nearby GOGPT plant given (moored offshore facility with no colocated land-based plant to compare against).
gogpt_candidate_basis: Vessel-mounted generation (FLNG-onboard, analogous to an FSRU) with no citable nameplate MW found for the as-installed Gimi gensets — per SOP §5, vessel-mounted generation with an undisclosed nameplate and unclear GOGPT-ontology fit is a REVIEWER CALL, not ADD or DO NOT ADD.
status_or_other_findings: Gimi FLNG: built 1976 as an LNG carrier, converted at Keppel Shipyard 2020-2023 (86% complete per the Aug 2022 update), departed the yard and arrived at the GTA site in early 2024, first gas/startup followed, chartered to BP through 2045, nameplate 2.7 mtpa / 2.45 mtpa output. Golar refinanced/re-leased Gimi FLNG in 2025 ($1.2bn) — financial/status items only, not acted on. Phase 2 (proposed, unit_id G100002066105) has no separate FLNG unit identified in the sources reviewed.
notes: This verdict covers the Gimi FLNG vessel serving Phase 1; no distinct captive-power finding is made for Phase 2, which remains proposed with no sourced facility detail.

captive_summary: New Fortress Energy's Mauritania 'energy hub' (MoU announced Dec 2021) is explicitly a gas-to-power supply scheme: NFE was to supply gas to the existing 180 MW Somolec power plant and fund a new 120 MW combined-cycle plant, with its Fast LNG output serving 'local gas and power markets as well as international exports.' This is the direction-test case — the terminal's purpose is piping gas OUT to external power stations, not powering itself with captive on-site generation. No source found describes any on-site captive generation at the terminal itself, and GEM's own record already carries the matching `PowerPlantsSupplied` relationship.
confirmed_how: LNG Prime's Dec 22, 2021 'New Fortress plans FLNG project off Mauritania' states NFE signed an MoU 'to develop an energy hub, including natural gas, power, LNG and blue ammonia,' under which NFE will 'supply natural gas to the existing 180 MW Somolec power plant and fund a new 120 MW combined cycle power plant,' with Fast LNG output serving 'local gas and power markets as well as international exports.' GEM's own field for this terminal already records `power_plants_supplied: Banda Gas-to-Power Project, Nouakchott Nord power plant`, consistent with the sourced direction of gas flow (OUT to power plants, not captive power IN to the terminal).

verification_log.note: confirms gas-to-power direction: Somolec 180 MW + new 120 MW plant

gogpt_prior_assessment: gogpt_prior = no; no nearby GOGPT plant given in this shard. The project's own target power plants (Somolec, 180 MW existing; a new NFE-funded 120 MW combined-cycle plant, referenced elsewhere as the Nouakchott Nord power plant) are the relevant GOGPT-side records, but matching/creating those is a GOGPT-side matter for the sibling gogpt-researcher repo, not this terminal's captive-power question.
